answers.answer: A quadrilateral is cyclic if two opposite angles are supplementary, or if an exterior angle at a vertex equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex.
solution: Case 1: if two opposite angles of a quadrilateral are supplementary (their sum is $180^\circ$), then the quadrilateral is cyclic (converse of theorem 3).
Case 2: if the exterior angle at a vertex of a quadrilateral equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex, then the quadrilateral is cyclic (corollary).
These are the two cases the lesson gives.
So a quadrilateral is cyclic in these two cases only: supplementary opposite angles, or an exterior angle equal to the interior opposite angle.

answers.answer: A quadrilateral is cyclic if: (1) two opposite angles are supplementary (sum 180°); (2) an exterior angle at a vertex equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex; (3) two adjacent vertices see the opposite side (equal angles on the same side of it) — i.e. two equal angles drawn on the same base on the same side, e.g. $m(\angle ABD)=m(\angle ACD)$; (4) a side subtends a right angle at the other two vertices (equal-angle special case, the side is a diameter); also, equivalently, there exists a point equidistant from all four vertices (the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet at one point).
